criteria.expectedOutcome: Synthetic CASREP workspace completes the named source obligation: all six actors, comments and return loop, revised immutable snapshots, five current-revision approvals, explicit local mock CO release, holder and audit visibility; INITIAL/UPDATE/CORRECT/CASCOR obey the disclosed invented grammar. Exact supplied messages and exports remain labeled synthetic. NWP conformance and operational authority remain unverified.

Wrong-role, skipped-role, stale-revision and duplicate/released transitions are rejected without changing successful audit. Editing B after EV-001-07 invalidates that approval and sets DRAFT; release is blocked until all five reviewers approve the new revision.

C and D branch from B and differ in repair. Display base 2026-10-13T18:00:00Z, left 2026-10-14T12:00:00Z and right 2026-10-15T12:00:00Z. Explicit left choice produces E with both parents, five retained revisions, no valid approvals and DRAFT; submit restarts at Division Officer.
Reviewer completes actual draft, submit, comment, return, revised save, resubmit, five approvals and explicit CO mock release, then downloads the saved message/audit package matching B.

Actual interactions walk mock INITIAL A through return to originator, corrected B, all five downstream reviewers and explicit CO mock release. Final RELEASED/NONE, two revisions, five current approvals and exact supplied synthetic export. Accessible live walkthrough guide and one-page fielding brief cover role permissions, classification handling, Navy messaging integration approach and fielding prerequisites; live execution remains a human review activity.

One workspace displays saved message, current revision, current holder, route and historical comments/approvals; full return-release path ends in a downloaded synthetic message/audit package, with no email or external release required for this local demonstration.
Fictional casualty impact and parts-priority narrative remain visible beside returned feedback; the sailor edits once and retains both versions. No measured readiness or time improvement is claimed.

CASREP is actually written, submitted, commented on, returned, revised to B and routed through the named six-role chain in one workspace, ending in explicit local mock release and matching message/audit export.

Drafting, comments, A/B revision history and complete chain-of-command decisions remain in one durable report workspace; return-release journey yields RELEASED/NONE and reload preserves all five valid approvals.
Requirements heading is preserved as source traceability; all child obligations map to six-role routing, four-type synthetic validation, history/audit, current holder and synthetic-only data checks.

All six named roles have comment capability on unreleased content; only originator edits/submits, downstream current holder returns or approves/forwards, CO approves then explicitly mock-releases. Self-return/CO-forward restrictions and unauthorized actor are visible and rejected server-side. Role selection is labeled simulation.

Exact supplied INITIAL, UPDATE, CORRECT and CASCOR texts parse and render; missing equipment, invalid type/category/timestamp/marking are rejected. A/B history, every comment and approval and routing/current holder remain inspectable. Invented grammar is fully disclosed; actual NWP 1-03.1 conformance remains unverified.

Only exact fictional supplied samples and labeled synthetic edits are used; every screen and message/audit export says Synthetic — not validated against the real CASREP format. Prohibited marking test rejects the fabricated placeholder.

Expected deliverables heading is preserved as traceability; child deliverables include actual six-role return/revision/mock-release journey, live walkthrough guide and one-page fielding brief, inspected through documentation journey.

Mock INITIAL A is saved/submitted, commented on and returned, revised to B, resubmitted, approved by Division Officer, Department Head, Engineer Officer/CHENG, XO and CO then explicitly mock-released. RELEASED/NONE, two revisions, five valid approvals, exact export and reload state are observable.

Live walkthrough guide and one-page fielding brief describe all six role permissions, classification boundary, Navy messaging integration approach and fielding prerequisites; both accessible in UI and delivered as documents.
Source is linked and quoted with original provenance intact.

steps.text: Live walkthrough: draft, return, revise, review and simulated CO release.
Demo roles simulate permissions; they do not authenticate users. Owner approval is required before delivery or deployment.
No Navy messaging connection. Fielding requires approved identity, message rules, classification handling, retention and release adapters.
